title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from this page and its neighbours): over a base, one has a rank-2 matrix family with two endomorphisms σ, ρ. They satisfy σ² = −1 and ρ² = ρ − 1, so ρ³ = −1; these are the order-4 and order-6 generators of a 2-dimensional SL₂(ℤ) = ℤ/4 *_{ℤ/2} ℤ/6 type representation. Further data are N = σ + ρ, N₀, N₁ and the idempotents ε₀ = 1 + N₀, ε₁ = 1 + N₁. Grothendieck wants to show that his conditions (51)–(56), essentially (64), imply condition (55): ε₀ and ε₁ are indecomposable in every fibre, i.e. N₀ and N₁ are non-collinear fibrewise.

Previous page: if N₁ = λN₀ on some fibre, then σ̃² = 1 and ρ̃³ = 1 give λ² = λ³ = 1, so λ = 1. Hence N₀ commutes with σ and ρ, so N commutes with them, so σ and ρ commute on that fibre.

This page finishes the contradiction under that commutativity.
1. (σ+ρ)² = σ² + ρ² + 2σρ = −1 + (ρ−1) + 2σρ.
2. The idempotence (σ+ρ)² = σ+ρ then gives 2σρ = σ + 2.
3. Multiplying by σ gives 2σ²ρ = σ² + 2σ, i.e. −2ρ = −1 + 2σ. So 2N = 1.
4. Taking determinants (rank 2): 4·det N = 1. But det N = 0 for a regular (rank-1) idempotent, so 0 = 1, absurd.
Conclusion: N₀ and N₁ are fibrewise non-collinear, so (55) follows from the other conditions, modulo the admitted step (64) ⇒ (68).

A crossed-out first attempt used traces of (**), with Tr σρ = 2, Tr σ = 0, Tr 1 = 2, and found no contradiction (4 = 4). It then tried determinants, using det σ = det ρ = 1, which follow from (64) when σ, ρ are regular (non-scalar).

Closing remark: Grothendieck conjectures an equivalent reformulation of (51)–(56), labelled (75): σ² + 1 = ρ² − ρ + 1 = 0 and ε₀ := −σ⁻¹ρ (= σρ) is a regular idempotent. The next page pursues this, wanting N = σ + ρ to be idempotent with Tr N = 1, det N = 0.

The content amounts to an elementary linear-algebra characterisation of certain 2-dimensional representations of the modular group in terms of idempotents; it is part of his 'équation des lacets' bookkeeping.
errors: The identity (σ+ρ)² = σ²+ρ²+2σρ is valid only because σ and ρ were shown to commute on the fibre (previous page). It is not valid in general; the page relies on that context implicitly.

The crossed-out (***) determinant computation looks garbled. Correctly, det(2σρ) = 4 and det(σ+2) = det σ + 2 Tr σ + 4 = 5, which would also give a contradiction (4 = 5, i.e. 1 = 0). The written formula does not match this and was abandoned.

The final step needs det N = 0, i.e. N regular. In fact 2N = 1 together with N² = N already gives 1 = 2·(2N) − ... ⇒ 1 = 0 (4N² = 1 and 4N = 2 give 1 = 2), so the contradiction holds even without regularity. A minor redundancy, not an error.

ideas.what: Showing that two rank-1 idempotents attached to the generators σ (σ² = −1) and ρ (ρ² − ρ + 1 = 0) of a rank-2 modular-group representation are fibrewise non-collinear, by reducing to the commuting case and deriving 2(σ+ρ) = 1, a contradiction
ideas.modern_name: Elementary linear algebra of 2-dimensional representations of SL₂(ℤ) = ℤ/4 *_{ℤ/2} ℤ/6 over a base ring (irreducibility / indecomposability conditions)
ideas.where_published: Related 'équation des lacets' material appears only in these unpublished notes, as far as known

ideas.what: Conjectural reformulation (75): the conditions (51)–(56) are equivalent to σ² + 1 = 0, ρ² − ρ + 1 = 0, and −σ⁻¹ρ being a regular idempotent
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of rank-2 modular-group representations via a pair of complementary idempotents

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures that his system (51)–(56) is equivalent to the compact form (75): σ²+1 = ρ²−ρ+1 = 0 with ε₀ = −σ⁻¹ρ a regular idempotent. The next page only begins to check this.
missed.quote: Je ne serais pas étonné qu'on ait aussi des conditions équivalentes à (51) à (56) dans C formes (75)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a minor, easily checkable linear-algebra statement. It is of interest only for reconstructing the 'équation des lacets' programme, not as new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine matrix algebra closing a case of a contradiction argument, plus a modest conjectural reformulation. There is nothing a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'donc la relation (σ+ρ)² = σ+ρ s'écrit' rather than 'dans la relation'.

In the crossed-out block, '(≠4)' may be '(f4)' / a reference; the (***) formula appears to read '2² = 2² + 2Tr σ + (det σ)²' or similar, struck out, with 'Tr σ' underbraced as 0 and the conclusion '1 = 0'.
The final step reads '4 det N = 1 i.e. 0 = 1, absurde', with det N underbraced 0.
Margin page number '471' at top; double vertical bar in the left margin next to the crossed-out block.
